Best thing about my setup? I have Windows reduced to a virtual machine thanks to unRAID 6.1.6. My next step will be to to mimic this and run two gamer systems on one comp (for friends). ....pft, who am I kidding, what friends.
Does running games in a VM have any impact on performance? Sounds like a neat setup.

Yes and no. Yes in the sense that instead of Windows having six cores with HT (12 logical cores) and 64GB of RAM, my Windows VM has been provisioned four logical cores and 32GB of RAM. Do I notice a performance hit though? No, I really don't -- that's what I mean by no. Also, I still have my duel R9 290s in crossfire setup; my performance in GTA5 is the same if not a bit better (probably due to my upgrade from win7 to win8.1). The one hitch I don't have ironed out completely is USB-PnP in Windows (which is not functional in Windows), I don't quite have my VM provisioned right on the on-board usb hub.

If you're considering this for your setup I recommend checking out the following first:

  • Does your system support VMT-d or AMD equivalent?
  • Check the forums first -- do research on your hardware. I found out there's an issue with Marvell SATA controllers halfway through my setup; my resolution was not using it and effectively leaving four sata ports on my motherboard I can't touch.
  • For windows, do you have Win8 or highter? You can VM win7, but Windows7 seemed to have an issue with crossfire; had perpetual I/O conflicts with second graphics card. Resolution was upgrading Windows; to be fair Lime Tech warned of issues VMing windows 7 and stated Windows 8 and above are supported. I don't like win8 but I loath win10 more -- lesser of two evils.
  • If you search the forums for your hardware do you find any issues? (basically above point again).
  • update your firmware, BIOS, and EFI before starting.
  • Be ready for a Plug-and-Pray experience; it's not plug-and-play but if you're a competent computer user who enjoys working on your own system everything is quite doable. I enjoy the tinkering aspects as much as I do gaming so this is a complete non-issue for me. If things go wrong be ready to ask for help in the forums, it seems to be a good/nice/strong community.
